So the Google credential key becomes the envelope object, breaking subsequent access_token/refresh_token reads on the next refresh regardless of credential-sharing config.

judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse envelope ({success, data}) and this code persists that envelope directly as the credential key, replacing the flat credential object that googleCredentialSchema.parse() previously returned. The first Google Calendar token refresh after this deploys writes {success:true, data:{...}} into Credential.key, so every subsequent GoogleCalendarService construction reads credential.key.access_token and credential.key.refresh_token as undefined and all Google Calendar operations fail for every user on every deployment, credential sharing enabled or not.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (the `{ success, data, error }` envelope), not the parsed token object (`.data`). However, in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh flow does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists it via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. That would store the envelope into `Credential.key` instead of the flat credential payload (previously produced by `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)`), breaking later reads that expect `credential.key.access_token` / `refresh_token` to exist at the top level. This defect is directly introduced by the diff.
